hook: Altman turned artificial intelligence from a research field into a consumer phenomenon and a geopolitical agenda item. ChatGPT's November 2022 launch under his leadership put generative AI in hundreds of millions of hands, and his Senate testimony six months later, a CEO asking to be regulated, set the tone for the global governance debate this library documents.
name: Sam Altman

quote.text: If this technology goes wrong, it can go quite wrong.
quote.context: Testimony to the U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee, May 16, 2023

moniker: The Face of the AI Boom

reading.body:
Sam Altman is the single figure most responsible for moving generative AI from a research context into mass public use and onto legislative agendas, doing both within roughly six months in 2022 and 2023.

The ChatGPT launch in November 2022 reached an estimated hundred million users in two months, a speed of adoption that had no prior consumer-product equivalent in the data. That scale of deployment created the demand signal that now pulls on compute, data-center construction, and grid capacity across the industry. The GPT APIs extended that pressure downstream, making frontier models the substrate for thousands of businesses and multiplying the number of organizations with a direct stake in AI infrastructure.

The Senate testimony and the November 2023 board crisis belong to a different register. Altman asking Congress for licensing and safety standards opened regulation as a mainstream legislative project, and his firing and reinstatement within five days exposed how fragile governance-by-charter can be at organizations where the stakes are this high. The data covers his leadership role, his public-facing moments, and the broad shape of the developer ecosystem he helped build. It does not cover OpenAI's compute agreements, power procurement, or capital structure, so the direct line from his decisions to specific infrastructure outcomes is not something this record establishes.
